territorial_scope.description: Applies within the Commonwealth of Kentucky; qualifying projects must also be located in a consolidated local government of at least 500,000 population.

evidence.quote: Encourage the location of data centers within the Commonwealth

summary.short: Kentucky HB 8 (2024) Sections 37-42 create a Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority approval process for qualified data center projects and exempt approved companies' data center equipment from sales and use tax under agreements of 15 to 50 years. Approved companies must report annually from September 1, 2025.
summary.long: Kentucky HB 8 (2024 RS) is a fiscal act; this copy contains Sections 37-42 and effective-date provisions (Sections 63-68), and omits Sections 1-36 and 43-62. Sections 37-41 create a data center incentive program in KRS Chapter 154, run by the Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority: eligible companies sign a memorandum of agreement, receive preliminary approval, then final approval once minimum capital investment is made. Qualifying projects need at least $450,000,000 of investment ($150,000,000 for a project organizer), sit in a consolidated local government of at least 500,000 residents, and may not replace existing Kentucky data centers except in listed cases. Section 42 (KRS Chapter 139) exempts approved companies' data center equipment from sales and use tax, excluding electricity. Agreement terms run 15 to 50 years. If investment falls short by the fifth anniversary, the exemption is revoked and tax is assessed. Approved companies report annually from September 1, 2025. The copy does not state the start date of Sections 37-42.

notes: Unofficial engrossed copy with broken line breaks; Sections 1-36 and 43-62 are omitted, so the effective date of Sections 37-42 is not in the excerpt. Internal inconsistencies: Section 37(17)(b)1 states 'fifty million dollars ($450,000,000)' while Section 37(18)(b)1 and Section 41(4)(b)1 use 'four hundred fifty million dollars'. The fifth-anniversary capital investment test runs from preliminary approval in Sections 37(10) and 41(3) and 41(11), but from the memorandum of agreement in Section 39(1)(e). Some definitions in Section 37(16) and 37(17) are fragmentary in this copy.
